reviewedFrom: EP02-01, EP02-03, EP02-04, EP02-05 and EP02-06 (docs/enterprise-production/completion-checklist.json); CLAUDE.md (division scope is the enforcement layer; a lot or home inherits its community's division); migrations 20261011010000_division_scope_rls_backstop and 20261011140000_division_hierarchy_integrity (restrictive division policies on projects, communities, lots, search_documents, tasks; project_division_history and project_division_at); lib/services/communities.ts (assertDivisionInCallerScope, requireCommunityScope); lib/services/team.ts (assertActorHoldsPermissions, assertDivisionGrantWithinReach, the live-member re-invite refusal, assertNotLastOrgAdmin, revokeSessionsOfDepartedMember, sweepQueuedAuthority); docs/reference/audit-trail.md (separation rules, critical audit rows, correlation ids); lib/financials/separation-of-duties.ts (BILL_SELF_APPROVAL_MESSAGE). EP02-08 (support access) is the browser journey journeys/support-access.spec.ts, not a subcase here. Fixture: one production builder — Gulf Coast (Cypress Landing: the two seeded takedown lots plus lots 21 and 22, developed; home 'Cypress Landing lot 1' on lot 21; task 'Cypress framing walk') and Treasure Coast (Seagrape Hammock: lots 1 and 2, developed; home 'Seagrape Hammock lot 1' on lot 1; task 'Seagrape framing walk'), each home, community, lot and task indexed for search — and a second organization with an owner and nothing else.

division-wall-holds.derivation: A superintendent (community.read, project.read) is limited by the owner to Gulf Coast (division_scope 'assigned', membership_divisions = Gulf Coast) and is on the project team of BOTH homes, so only the division stands between them and Treasure Coast. Division scope is the enforcement layer: services filter by it (listCommunities/getCommunity resolve the division scope; listProjects intersects with division-scoped project ids) and the restrictive policies back it on projects (member_can_reach_project), communities and lots (division_id in the member's divisions), and tasks and search_documents (project in member_reachable_project_ids). So the member gets Gulf Coast's home, community and task and none of Treasure Coast's: getCommunity and the inventory (which calls getCommunity) refuse as 'Community not found', the status chips count 0 lots, and neither search returns a Treasure Coast record. Raw reads with the member's own session return Gulf Coast's 1 home, 1 community, 4 lots, 1 task and 5 search documents (home, community, task, lots 21 and 22) and 0 of every Treasure Coast row. The header search (GET /api/search?q=) searches the fast types (project, task, ... — not community or lot); a typed search (?types=project,community,lot,task) includes them. The owner (an org admin, unscoped) is the control: both divisions' rows exist, Treasure Coast's community and inventory open, its 2 lots are counted, the header search finds its home and task and the typed search its home, community, lots and task. Searching never changes what a document belongs to: a home's search document keeps project_id = the home after any search (reindexEntity writes it that way; the wall reads it). Another organization's owner reaches nothing of this builder: every service list is empty of it, getCommunity is 'Community not found', and every raw read is 0 (search_documents_access requires membership of the row's org).

division-move-keeps-history.derivation: Harbor Point (Treasure Coast, lots 1 and 2, home 'Harbor Point lot 1' on lot 1, created in Treasure Coast) is moved by the owner to Gulf Coast with updateCommunity. communities_cascade_division moves its lots and home in the same statement, so the returned community, both lots and the home all read Gulf Coast. tg_projects_division_history closes the home's open Treasure Coast row and opens a Gulf Coast row; project_division_at(home, a moment before the move) is Treasure Coast and at now() Gulf Coast. A superintendent limited to Gulf Coast did not reach the home or the community before the move and reaches both after it (their division now contains them). Moving it back reverses all of it: everything reads Treasure Coast, history is Treasure (closed), Gulf (closed), Treasure (open), and the member loses the home, the community ('Community not found') and every raw row of the home. Each move records community.updated with from/to and homes_moved = 1 (lot 1 carries the one home).

limited-member-cannot-move-a-community-o.derivation: A land manager (community.write) limited to Gulf Coast. updateCommunity and createCommunity check the target division against the caller's scope (assertDivisionInCallerScope) and refuse a division outside it as 'Division not found', so moving Cypress Landing to Treasure Coast and creating 'Driftwood Cay' there are refused. Seagrape Hammock is outside their scope, so requireCommunityScope refuses touching it as 'Community not found'. Going straight to PostgREST with their own session, the communities restrictive policy's WITH CHECK rejects the new row (division not theirs): error 42501. Editing Cypress Landing's description in place is allowed (they do hold community.write in Gulf Coast). Afterwards nothing moved: Cypress Landing, its lots and its home are Gulf Coast, Seagrape Hammock is Treasure Coast, and no Driftwood Cay exists.

invites-cannot-escalate.derivation: The inviter is a land manager limited to Gulf Coast holding members.manage by an explicit grant (every built-in role with members.manage is an org admin — org_owner, org_admin, org_office_admin — and admins are exempt by design, so this is the only shape of a non-admin inviter). inviteTeamMember checks, before anything is created: (1) the inviter must hold every key of the target role, else 'You cannot grant access you do not hold yourself (...)' (the key list is dropped from the comparison: it is the first three missing keys in database order) and the denial is written to authorization_audit_log through authorize() with resource_type 'membership' and resource_id = the target role's id — one 'deny' each for org_owner and org_admin; (2) a division-limited inviter cannot invite with division scope 'all' ('You are limited to your own divisions...') nor into a division they lack ('You can only assign divisions you belong to.'); (3) an email that is already an active member is refused ('This person is already an active member...') and their role, status and scope are untouched. No app_users row and no invited membership is created by any refused invite.

expected.inviteOwner: You cannot grant access you do not hold yourself. Ask an organization administrator.
expected.inviteAdmin: You cannot grant access you do not hold yourself. Ask an organization administrator.
expected.inviteAllDivisions: You are limited to your own divisions, so you can only invite people into divisions you hold.
expected.inviteIntoTreasure: You can only assign divisions you belong to.
expected.reinviteActiveMember: This person is already an active member. Change their role from the team list instead of inviting them again.

departure-cancels-queued-authority.derivation: A bookkeeper (bill.read) with, as fixtures, one active recurring invoice they created, one pending outbox job whose payload names them as actor (and one the owner queued), one payment_run_approvers seat and one auth session. Before: they read the Gulf Coast home's payables. The owner suspends them (members.manage). updateMemberStatus revokes their sessions because they have no other active membership (revoke_user_sessions deletes 1), and sweepQueuedAuthority deactivates their invoice schedule (1), fails their pending job with 'Cancelled: the member who queued this job left the organization.' (1; the owner's job stays pending), deletes their approver seat (1) and finds no report schedules or device tokens (0, 0) with no failed step; the member_suspended event carries exactly those counts. After: the membership is suspended and authorize() refuses them bill.read. The owner is then the only active org admin (org_owner; the accountant and the production roles are not admins), so suspending the owner's own membership is refused by assertNotLastOrgAdmin and the owner stays active.

job.last_error: Cancelled: the member who queued this job left the organization.

lastAdmin.attempt: This is the last administrator for the organization. Assign another admin before changing or removing this one.

enterer-cannot-approve-own-bill.derivation: An office admin (bill.write and bill.approve) enters a $1,250 framing payable on the Gulf Coast home; it is saved pending. Rule bill.enterer_cannot_approve: the person who keyed it in may approve only if nobody else who holds bill.approve can reach the project; the owner can, so the clerk's approval is refused with BILL_SELF_APPROVAL_MESSAGE and one authorization_audit_log row is written (decision deny, reason_code deny_separation_of_duties, context.rule bill.enterer_cannot_approve) carrying a request (correlation) id. The payable stays pending. The owner approves it (approvedCount 1, status approved); approve_vendor_bills_with_outcomes writes the audit row in the same transaction, and its correlation_id comes from the x-correlation-id header the service client sends, so it is not null.

expected.selfApproval: You entered this payable, so someone else has to approve it.

lost-audit-is-never-a-clean-success.derivation: docs/reference/audit-trail.md lists 'Commitment issue (approval): updateCommitment when status becomes approved — critical audit'. With the audit table refusing this org's commitment rows (an injected trigger), the owner approves a $58,000 draft purchase order: the change commits (status approved), the audit insert fails, is retried once and fails again, so the complete row is queued as one pending audit_retry outbox job (entity commitment, action update, after_data.status approved, actor the owner, with its correlation id) and the action reports AuditRecordPendingError(retryQueued=true): 'The change was saved, but its audit record is still pending. It has been reported and will be written automatically.' No audit row for the approval exists while the fault stands. Once the fault is removed the outbox writes the row: the job completes and exactly one audit row exists (update, by the owner, status approved) with the same correlation id as the queued row.

expected.approval: The change was saved, but its audit record is still pending. It has been reported and will be written automatically.
